classifications.reason: The nested vehicle definition excludes devices moved by human power, matching the bicycle contract.
The passenger-capacity contract supplies no incompatible wheel, engine or speed requirement that would rule out every member under the open phrase “or similar vehicle.”
The words do not settle whether a motorized wheelchair used by a child can qualify as a vehicle similar to a motor-driven scooter or cycle.
Commercial licensing does not require two or three wheels, so the definition's allowance of fewer than two wheels prevents the quoted ru.moped contract from providing complete coverage.
The controlling definition expressly names electric bicycles among the classes the term does not include.
The controlling definition expressly names electric scooters among the classes the term does not include.
Emergency designation supplies no two-wheel minimum, whereas the admitting words permit fewer than two wheels and the proposed covering contract requires two or three.
The fire-fighting-vehicle contract does not establish that every admitted member has the two or three wheels required by ru.moped.
The contract expressly ties its low-power two- or three-wheelers to the jurisdiction's classification, supplied here by the controlling moped definition.
The admitting words permit a qualifying one-wheeled self-propelled vehicle, which the motor-vehicle contract does not exclude but the ru.moped contract does not cover.
An admitted motorcycle already has two or three wheels under its contract and must satisfy the jurisdiction's moped requirements, placing every admitted member within ru.moped.
Official road service and identifying equipment impose no two-wheel minimum, so the quoted ru.moped contract does not cover every vehicle the admitting words permit.
The pedestrian contract includes motorized-wheelchair users, and the words do not settle whether their wheelchairs qualify under “or similar vehicle.”
The cane, guide-animal or assistance condition does not resolve whether a motorized wheelchair used by such a pedestrian falls within “or similar vehicle.”
The exception requires exclusive use upon stationary rails, while the on-track-equipment contract does not establish that exclusivity for every member.
School-service designation and markings add no wheel, engine or speed restriction that establishes incompatibility with every qualifying “similar vehicle.”
The marked passenger-for-hire contract does not require two or three wheels, leaving qualifying vehicles outside the proposed ru.moped coverage.
The tour-or-shuttle-bus branch of the contract supplies no wheel, engine or speed restriction that rules out every vehicle admitted by “or similar vehicle.”
The words do not establish that a qualifying towing unit makes the combination itself a moped or that every admitted combination satisfies the covering contract.
Public-transit service and identifying displays do not establish any incompatibility between the bus contract and every vehicle admitted by “or similar vehicle.”
A purpose-built goods-carrying body does not rule out a qualifying motor-driven cycle or similar vehicle, and the contract supplies no incompatible wheel, engine or speed requirement.
